text:
Recent research supports separating perceived relevance from immediate consumption intent: a 2025/2026 movie-recommendation study measured these separately and found that history-based explanations could improve viewing intention, with benefits depending on preference alignment. References to past items helped understanding but could become redundant. For this task, an actionable annotation scheme would independently record “generally relevant,” “would choose now,” and an evidence-supported connection to a specific recent-history item; these are proposed operationalizations, not validated measures from that study. [Contextualizing Recommendation Explanations](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/ICWSM/article/view/42667).

Abstention should remain distinct from rejection. Research on biased non-response shows that missing labels can systematically distort learning; silence or inability to identify an item should therefore remain unknown, rather than become negative preference evidence. Record explicit rejection reasons only when stated; compatibility, ownership, mood and other unavailable attributes remain unknown. Retain the supporting feedback excerpt for each code and report uncertainty/abstention coverage alongside acceptance and rejection rates. [Active Learning with Biased Non-response](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10618-024-01026-x).

For twenty users, a practical exploratory protocol is independent double-coding, a pilot codebook, preserved pre-adjudication labels and documented disagreements. Assess agreement between coders interpreting the same feedback—not agreement between users’ preferences. Report label counts, raw agreement and an appropriate chance-corrected coefficient with uncertainty; recommendations within users are clustered observations. Recent annotation work emphasizes confidence intervals and disagreement patterns, while small-sample research cautions that conventional alpha estimates and bootstrap intervals can perform poorly. These diagnostics support auditability, not population-wide conclusions. [Counting on Consensus (2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.06865), [Improved Inference for Krippendorff’s Alpha (2024)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0378375824000272).
